title: Understanding the Project Structure
description: Deep dive into settings.py, urls.py, and other important files.

slides.title: settings.py – The Heart ❤️
slides.content:
# Configuration Central

`settings.py` holds all your project’s configuration:

- **`INSTALLED_APPS`** – List of all Django apps in your project.
- **`DATABASES`** – Database connection settings (SQLite by default).
- **`TEMPLATES`** – How templates are loaded and rendered.
- **`MIDDLEWARE`** – Security and request/response processing.
- **`STATIC_URL`** – URL to serve static files (CSS, images).

You’ll modify this file often as your project grows.

quizData.question: Which setting lists all the Django apps that are enabled in your project?
quizData.explanation: `INSTALLED_APPS` is a tuple of all app names that Django knows about. You must add any custom app you create to this list.

slides.title: urls.py – The Navigator 🧭
slides.content:
# URL Routing

`urls.py` maps URLs to views. A simple entry looks like:

```python
from django.urls import path
from . import views

urlpatterns = [
    path('', views.home, name='home'),
]
```

When a user visits `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`, Django calls the function `home()` from the `views` module.

quizData.question: Which file defines how URLs are mapped to views?
quizData.explanation: `urls.py` contains the `urlpatterns` list that directs incoming requests to the appropriate view functions or classes.

slides.title: Other Key Files 🔑
slides.content:
## `wsgi.py` / `asgi.py`

These are entry points for web servers (like Gunicorn, uWSGI) to serve your Django app. For now, you don’t need to modify them.

## `__init__.py`

An empty file that tells Python that the folder is a Python package. It allows you to import modules from that folder.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use the Django shell to explore

Run `python manage.py shell` to interact with your project’s code. It’s a great way to test things quickly.
